why: the faint text tier is dark enough to clear 4.5:1 on the paper and on the card stock
the four desk inks: a stroke stores the ink NAME, and --ink-walnut equals --ink-stroke so a stroke with no ink paints the same; Flux inherits the four
a card-scoped ink pair: the card stock stays cream in every theme, so card text cannot follow --ink-on-paper, which flips light on a dark page
card footer, badge and excerpt inks: one value each, readable on the cream card stock in every theme
--choice colours a chosen, pressed or selected state: brass in Arbor, cyan in Flux
the active mode tab: brightened ink and a 1px olive hairline, no brass fill; a token, so the hue can change without touching a component
the help "?" colour, never brass (brass means the current choice); Arbor aliases --accent-rest, Flux sets its own
the door olive: --accent-rest is too faint on the paper, so doors use a darker step of the same olive, set per theme with the paper they sit on
one token for the frame's side gutter, read by the host's padding and by the strip's negative offset, so the two cannot drift apart
the paper fills the stage height: the chrome budget is the host's fixed chrome above and below the grid (40 + 63 + 16 + 48 px, hand-synced; fx3.mjs measures it), the fence is the gap under the paper
the rhizome's rest colour: one step above the desk ground, barely visible; a token, so a theme reskins it in one place
the roots are the house olive, stepped down to --accent-door on the cream page so they still read behind the words
each theme's default writing face; the face list reads this token, so its label cannot drift from what renders
square corners everywhere: the radius slots are 0
Scrollbars, app-wide: thin, quiet, square and theme-toned. Declared on every element, not only :root, because scrollbar-width does not reliably inherit in Chromium
the standard properties are the one scrollbar mechanism: Chromium 121+ ignores ::-webkit-scrollbar wherever they are set; the width is native thin (10px or less)
paper and card scroll regions take the paper family's subdued pair; the board canvas sits on the paper, so it joins the paper pair
the one exception: .mode-scroll sits inside the scaled page, so its bar is the webkit mechanism at 10px divided by the applied scale, painted back to 10px; @supports keeps Firefox on thin
the padding keeps the text column one width at every scale: the margin cancellation plus 10px less the bar, with the bar capped at 10 layout px
ground
the teal twin of --lamp-glow, so the backdrop is not Arbor brown under Flux
the room reads blue: every dark surface sits near hue 212; the warmth overlay grows with typing
a card is dark glass, and so are its pop-up and the deck wizard, in both page tones
Flux's "?" colour: teal, never brass or olive
Flux's default writing face is Titillium Web
the door colour follows the ground: on Flux's dark glass it is the palette's text accent, never olive
the faint text tier is darkened one step down the teal ramp to clear 4.5:1 on the paper and on the card stock

MACHINA - the third theme, strictly additive under [data-theme='machina'] (docs/theme-foundations/machina/machina-foundations.md, docs/plans/machina-build.md). Two casts: COOL is the base block, NEUTRAL lists only what changes. The page pref flips only the paper and card tokens; the chrome stays dark. Orange is scarce in both casts. --text-low is lifted above the mockup's muted value to clear the 4.5:1 text floor
Machina's default writing face

Finalize and the Plan door are plain: quiet at rest, --text-hi on hover; the carrier colour only where it means current. Orange is for the notch, the closed strip and a chosen state, never a resting label
the mark: WRIZ in the content-label face and the outlined square in the active carrier (steel in COOL, orange in NEUTRAL); Arbor's PNG mask is switched off as Flux's is
the vignette sits behind the content: it shades the room, never the page

FLUX V2 - the shell: the rules that are not just a token. Orange is scarce (the caret, the sprint surge, Uplink, the mark, the current item's left bar); every other selected state is cyan, because --brass is cyan under Flux. The frame's edge, grid, brackets and readouts are an overlay ring that recedes with the chrome; nothing here changes the page's size or position
the rail's hover and active states are electric blue (--line-active): no brown tile, no olive, no brass

FLUX V2 - the screens: every input reads the Flux glass (never Arbor brown); Flux shows its own orange WRIZO mark top left; a board card is a dark-glass node, its tokens re-pointed inside the canvas only; the rail's place block wraps
Flux marks a card's first line by colour only: capitals, spacing or another face would widen the line and make the card taller; a skin changes only the skin
the arrival's Write door is the choice colour (cyan), not brass: orange keeps only its fixed homes
the card's resize and connect corner and the drop target are the choice colour (cyan): a handle on a selected node is a choice, and orange is scarce
one line with an ellipsis; the full name is the button's title

GLITCH METER (docs/briefs/flux-flicker-meter-brief.md; components/GlitchMeter.tsx): Flux's progress animation over the whole screen, never while typing. Its own layer portalled to body: fixed, no pointer events, no layout; above the page and chrome, below the block caret (60). Its Signal Loss events are the ambient texture's .theme-fx-* elements at the meter's intensity (--op)

the still: a faint scan-and-grain overlay, opacity = intensity x 0.42, no motion; under reduced motion the global rule makes it simply appear; the 2.4s ease is for Ambiance 0, where that rule does not apply
one caret: !important, because the editor sets its pen ink as an inline caret colour, which would leave the native line drawn over the orange block
themed, never an Arbor literal (the same move as .wz-splash-veil)

the vignette sits behind the content in every theme, so it shades the room, never the page; one rule, so a theme added later cannot bring the band back. isolation:isolate on body keeps it visible above the lamp background (page-size.mjs V, MV and V-room check it from paint)
the hint in each theme's own type: Arbor's italic prose serif, Flux and Machina their upright content face; on the framed prose page it stands on the page, clear of the text

the front door's wordmark, tagline and doors stay hidden while the splash holds (Splash.tsx sets the attribute) and fade in as it leaves; transition:none makes the hide instant, the base rule's transition still governs the reveal
pointer-events:none so a hidden door cannot be pressed (opacity never gates hit-testing); focus and keys are unaffected
the board: square corners, brass only on selection. A card is stacked stock: lighter than the board, a 1px hairline, a 2px hard edge and a soft shadow
the board canvas joins the paper-toned scrollbar group: it sits on --paper, a light surface, so the dark default would not suit it
the wrap paints the board surface (--paper), so the bars in its gutter and below it sit on the surface their paper-toned thumb was chosen for; background only, no geometry moves
the move cursor over a card: pure affordance, the drag itself is BoardEditor.tsx's; the pin, handle and layer toggle are siblings, so the browser resolves their own cursors and no exclusion is needed
the resize handle: a 10px solid brass square with no border, centred on the card's corner (-5px); a diagonal cursor, since it resizes freely on both axes and shows only on the selected box
while a card's corner is held the whole canvas wears the diagonal resize arrow, so a pointer that lags the corner never flips to the I-beam

THE BOARD-CARD (PW2 S2): a nested board on its parent's canvas, riding the same .board-pin box a page does. Its kind is told by shape, never colour: a doubled edge drawn by ::before at z-index -1. No isolation here on purpose: a new stacking context would trap the pseudo-element in front of the card

the olive pin, the connection grab at the card's top-left on every card: a circle (the one exception to square corners, as .status-dot), olive because it is a connection, never brass. A domed sphere-top: an off-centre highlight lit from the top left, as the card's shadow is, darkening to a hand-computed olive rim; the 1px border keeps the dome contained (fx5.mjs S5 asserts the radius)
the grabbing cursor while a move-drag is held: a canvas-level data-dragging flag, read as data-thread-armed is; board-wide, since only one drag is ever in flight

fit to text: a small square icon on a hand-sized card beside the resize grip; shown on hover or focus (a real button, so Tab reaches it), receding with the chrome; guidance colour at rest, --choice only while pressed; square, flat, no shadow; its words from the lexicon
line widths: lines 1px, the arm 1.25px, a selected line 2px; non-scaling-stroke keeps them true if the board's svg is scaled

the close X sits at the strip's right end, the card's top-right corner, in the card's own ink (it sits on the cream stock, not the page); the editor's bottom padding takes the room a foot used to give

the screenplay sheet is a page of its own: US Letter at 12pt, where 1in = 6em and Courier's 1ch = 0.6em, so the page (51em by 66em), the margins (9em left, 6em right, top and bottom), the 60ch measure and the 1em line all follow from one number. Every dimension is em, so changing that number scales the whole sheet as one object and the grid never reflows. box-sizing:border-box makes width:51em the page including its margins; height is exact, so every sheet in the sequence is the same page

the scaling is one-directional: true size (816px, 12pt) is the most a page ever is, never multiplied by --paper-scale (a screenplay page is a physical reference); below 816px of room the min() arm scales the whole page as one object

THE SEQUENCE, and the gap between sheets: the gap is chrome, never body. In rem, never the sheet's em, so it does not scale with the paper; not a multiple of --script-line (1.5 lines at 24px), so no one can mistake it for blank lines; and flex gap, so nothing can render into it (sc2.mjs asserts none does). align-items:stretch keeps each sheet filling the column

the line unit, and the rules that keep the render wrapping as store/scriptLedger.ts counts (sc2.mjs compares the two): --script-line is one line box, so N blank lines render as N line-heights; overflow-wrap:anywhere breaks an over-long word at the measure; hyphens:none, because a hyphenating browser would break every count

the first element of a page contributes no space above it: here at document start, and the paginator applies the same rule at every page top (store/scriptLedger.ts reports intrinsic spacing, so it stays position-independent); it also keeps the sheet from being pushed down by a first child's margin
the vertical seam splitting the strip into writing and delivery groups
a selected mode tab is where-you-are, not an act: olive marks state, brass stays for events; no fill, no brass
the narrow layout follows the full recede
the bar's fill is --chrome-surface, the chrome token every theme overrides (--ink-900 is Arbor's raw surface and would leave this strip half-themed)

the scrollbar is flush with the paper's outer right edge: a scrollbar renders at its element's border box, so .mode-scroll extends its box across the page's right padding with a negative margin and puts the same amount back as its own padding (the text stays where it was). Both read --wz-page-pad-x, the page's own margin setting, so the cancellation is exact at every margin

the typewriter fade is monotonic: the topmost line sits at the floor through --tw-fade-start, then the ramp climbs to fully shown over --tw-fade-band, so no newer line is ever fainter than an older one (typewriter-fade.mjs)
three selectors (an attribute and two classes), so the celebrate fill wins over the lime base rule whatever the source order

the strip is flush at the screen's left edge while the paper stays centred in the viewport: the strip is out of the grid's flow (position:absolute), the host's padding is symmetric (--frame-host-pad-x) and the strip's negative offset cancels it with the same token, so the two cannot drift; leftover width splits evenly around the paper (fx5.mjs S10)
the strip hangs flush off the top bar's dividing line: top:-16px cancels the spacer the editors render under the bar, and the strip drops its own top border and corner rounding

the strip must win its own band: z-index:1, so the stage that follows it in the DOM cannot cover it for a real pointer. Geometry would move the paper, which never reflows for chrome; 1 is the smallest value that beats auto, and nothing else legitimately overlaps the strip

Trash reaches the foot: min-height does not make a height definite, so the strip's height:100% fell back to auto; this element is a flex column and the strip takes flex:1, so its foot's margin-top:auto has room to push against (item137.mjs)
the script page mounts the same .mode-pagecol geometry prose uses, at the same width band, so the paper's measure is the one constant; Courier's ch measures are relative to the sheet's own font size

THE PROSE PAGE IS A LETTER PAGE, in page units (docs/plans/page-size.md): 8.5 x 11 page-inches, margins in page-inches (pageDress.ts), type in points (fontSize.ts). One number, --wz-letter-in, written on this stage from its size (store/pageScale.ts), scales all three, so the page grows in shape only and every line breaks where it did; the value here is scale 1, for the first paint. Every anchor reads --wz-page-w / --wz-page-half

the page lays out at scale 1 always and is painted at --wz-k by a transform (below), so every line breaks where it does at 1366; the anchors read the painted width (--wz-anchor-w, --wz-page-half), the zoomed width while zoomed
a definite height, so the letter-tall page shrinks to the stage instead of growing the column past it

the prose page: letter height capped to the stage (a flex item that may shrink; the text scrolls inside it); margins in page-inches (normal 1in, narrow 0.684, wide 1.526), top and bottom 0.85in. --paper-scale:1 inside the page, because page units carry the scale here; --wz-page-pad-x is the finished margin the scrollbar cancellation reads
the layout height DeskFrame computes (letter, or what the stage holds once painted at --wz-k); the transform paints it at k

THE ZOOM: the same page transformed by --wz-zoom (1.6, capped to the stage's width), scale never reflow, so its layout box and every line break stay as in the normal view. The column widens to the stage so the band mask spans the zoomed page. THE BAND, in line-heights (--tw-lh) from the anchor at 50% of the column (--tw-lead keeps the .12 stop 56px or more from the top): 0 at the top, .12 / .40 / .72 at 6.6 / 4.2 / 2.2 lines above, full from 0.15 above to 1.45 below, .40 at 2.8 below, 0 from 4.4 below. Text and paper fade into the desk together; this band replaces the scroller's top mask

while zoomed the Sliver keeps DRAWER_MIN by growing rightward from its anchor, over the zoomed band (a tool overlays, nothing is displaced); never leftward, under the strip; its grip stays on top, so it still closes
while zoomed the column fills the stage: .mode-stage is a content-sized flex item, so a 100% column inside it would stay narrow and the band mask would cut the enlarged page at its sides
the middle (the engine writes the same value from ZOOM_ANCHOR)

the script sheet grows to fill a short script's column (flex-grow on the sheet, flex-shrink 0 so a long script is never compressed; the scroll-cap scrolls it). The scroll-cap itself takes no main-axis flex-grow, mirroring .mode-stage: its width stays content-sized so the stage can centre the page, and the height fill comes from cross-axis stretch; min-width:0 and max-width:100% guard overflow near the floor (fx7.mjs S1)

the sliver's anchor is absolutely positioned inside the stage, so it can never move the paper in any state. Its right edge lands on the paper's left edge, so the grip never enters the text measure; its width is clamped to the margin between the Drawer's right edge and the paper (--frame-gap is the fixed remainder), dipping at most --sliver-paper-pad (38px, hand-synced with .mode-page's padding) into the paper's padding, never the text: clamp(160px, margin + padding, 200px)
raised above a busy board's cards, which outrank z-index 5 within this stage's context; the panel is inset 16px, so its grip needs no separate lift

the screenplay anchors ride the page itself: half of 8.5in scaled by the column's own token, floored at the stage's half (the min(50%, ...) idiom --board uses) so a clamped page cannot push the anchor off the stage

the board narrows beside an open drawer: BoardEditor writes --board-l, --board-r and --board-strip on the stage, and the anchors read the board's real edges, so the Tools tab sits on the board's left edge with the room the board left it

z-index 56 over 55: within the stage's isolated context a board's cards rank too, and box.z climbs unbounded, so the drawer sits in the stage's safely-above-content tier (.board-create-ghost's 50), the grip one above its panel

a pop-out on the page never extends past the page surface: the page's drawers end at its foot (--wz-page-foot, written by DeskFrame) and scroll inside; where the page runs past the stage (the zoom), at the stage's foot
the Tutor's tab rides the board's right edge, its panel standing against it
raised with the grip anchor above, one below it
the Tutor panel's width is a reading measure, clamp(320px, 34vw, 460px), declared once so the open rule and the docked rule's ceiling read the same value

THE BAR COMES HOME: the progress instrument renders under the page in the rhizome's lane, inside the 40px fence the stage already reserves (--fx3-paper-fence), as an absolutely positioned descendant of an overlay anchor, so the paper's rect is immune to it. The track spans the paper's width at every scale (the goal-glow anchor's measure math); pointer-events:none, so an instrument can never become a control

THE GOAL RHIZOME: the anchor sits behind the paper (z-index -1), the roots in --rhizome-ink. The field's viewBox equals its pixel size, so 1 user unit is 1 CSS px; no vector-effect, since non-scaling-stroke can break the pathLength draw-on in Chromium

while typing, everything off the page goes to 0: on the framed desk the floor is 0 (--fade-min lives only on .mode-stage, never an ancestor here), and the chrome outside the dissolve classes (the wordmark, the ember dot, the progress lane, the glitch meter) recedes with it, keyed on data-wz-writing; it returns on the engine's curve (--fade-dur)
the recede's exceptions: the page, the drawer tab arrows, progress strips that are on, and docked panels

the unified mode strip: its own class family so ModeSwitcher.tsx cannot drift under it; no brass, the active tab is brightened ink and a 1px olive hairline; uppercase and letterspacing are presentation only (text-transform), the DOM keeps the title-case strings
the mode tabs sit directly in the sprint-nav with no box of their own, so no second line is drawn under its bottom line
the "?" sits beside a tab, never inside it (a button cannot nest a button): an inline-flex wrapper reads the pair as one unit without changing the strip's gap

THE POP-OUT HOLD: a foot pop-out fades after fifteen words written or a period entered, never on a clock (Sliver.tsx sets data-popout-hold). It adds no fade: while the flag stands it out-specifies the two recede rules (0,5,0 and 0,4,0 over 0,3,0 and 0,2,0), and [data-open='true'] keeps a closed drawer closed

THE SLIDING LAYER, shared by both side drawers: the menu slides out from behind its tab and fades in together. The panel is the clip and the scroller and keeps the fade; the visible box and the slide live on this layer, on their own tokens, never --fade-dur

the contents are not live until the slide settles: for --drawer-dur the sliding layer takes no pointer input, so an early press does nothing rather than hit a neighbour (scripts/evidence/click-mid-open.mjs); an animation, because pointer-events is discrete; focus is unaffected
THE TAB ROW: the chosen tab and the drawer's arrow tab both mark where you are, so both are olive; brass stays for action controls
pointer events back on the "?" itself, because the row is pointer-events:none and a real press would otherwise land on nothing
this row's stretch-to-the-margins override, scoped by specificity (two classes) so it wins over the shared .wz-drawer-note rules whatever the order

REDUCED MOTION: fade only, short, no slide. The two panels carry their own !important duration, because the global floor (every transition 0.01ms !important) would flatten the fade, and opacity is not motion; a class selector out-ranks the floor's universal selector. The sliding layer is not exempt: it stays instant

the Structure zone's sub-labels and the rule between its halves: one zone reads as two, so a kind chip named Screenplay is never mistaken for the conversion door. Quieter than .wz-sliver-h; no accent (a sub-label is neither a state nor an act); the chips reuse .wz-page-setup-chip
the sliver's eyebrow labels are information, not events: quiet, neither olive nor orange
the engraved zone heading is the menus' one resting accent: olive
a row name's "?" sits beside its row, never inside it: the wrap is the flex row, and .wz-template-row keeps filling it
brass on the press, and brass at rest on the template the page already is (aria-pressed): brass marks a choice made

the scoped Typeface section: two scopes over the roster as a list; brass marks the scope in force and its current face (none for a mixed highlight); a dead Selection is dimmed and inert; choosing is the preview, no Apply; nothing moves the page
a scope label is never cut: each button is as wide as its label and grows to share the row; when the two cannot sit side by side, the second wraps under the first. No ellipsis
an ON toggle is a where-you-are state, so it rests olive (brass stays for the :active flash); the knob is --ink-950 for contrast on olive

the progress bar's line is shared with Full screen: one flex row with align-items:center puts the hairline and the toggle on one line by layout, never by nudged margins (the probe checks the centres within 0.6px); the hairline flexes, the toggle does not; min-width:0 lets it shrink

the Tutor panel moves exactly as the tool pop-out (.wz-sliver-panel): the same opacity and transform transition on --fade-dur (.2s fallback, ease), only the nudge mirrored; its width is static (the clamp, a custom property), never part of the transition; closed, it is invisible and inert whatever its footprint

min-height:0, because as a real flex item its default min-height:auto could grow it past its box with a long lens section, scrolling the document instead of the panel (the same escape .desk-frame-stage uses)

three regimes, set by Tutor.tsx's measure-effect from the true margin (stage right minus paper right): on a writing surface with 280px or more it occupies the margin at min(margin, open-w), flush to the paper; with less it overlays at open-w; on a board it keeps open-w and may overlay. The clamp here is only the fallback before the effect runs
the link dock's reader (a linked card or page, read-only, beside the page): square, no shadow, the theme's own words and tokens; its words select and copy as plain text
the board regime: the board is an arrangement surface, not paper, so its Tutor panel keeps open-w and may overlay the canvas; Tutor.tsx leaves the width to this rule on a board

a closed drawer is hidden whatever the dissolve says: visibility:hidden (no opacity can bring it back; it leaves the tab order), plus opacity 0 at a higher specificity in both dissolve contexts. The close still fades and slides: visibility flips after the longer of --fade-dur and --drawer-dur; opening shows at once
a closing drawer fades on the drawer's own duration, not the writing dissolve's slow --fade-dur, so a keystroke-closed Tutor fades as fast as the Tools drawer
under reduced motion the closed panel fades on --drawer-dur-reduced and is hidden when that is done; the delay holds the hide back
the dock toggle: a small quiet icon-only corner control, sized like the drawer note's "?"
DrawerNote.tsx's CSS, the one definition every caller shares; the tab row's override lives beside .wz-drawer-tabnotes, scoped by specificity
a note beside an uppercase heading would inherit its transform; a note's words are never a heading, so it is reset here once
near the right edge the pop opens leftward from the button's right edge (DrawerNote.tsx measures at open time), so it stays inside the viewport

HELP BUTTONS (store/help.ts, HelpButton/HelpPop; docs/mockups/help-buttons/index.html): one shared overlay, position:fixed in a body portal, so it can never move or resize the page it sits over. --help (never brass) means more words available

the conversation renders under the head and has no scrollbox of its own: the panel scrolls as one column, a bubble grows to its content, and no second scrollbar exists in this subtree (fx10.mjs S1 asserts it)

the Free Write roster and its one standing draw, only in Free Write (absent elsewhere). Zero resting orange: presets rest olive, brass on hover, --brass-press on press. Figtree, since these label presets and never become the writer's words. No overflow of any kind (the panel scrolls as one column; fx10.mjs checks); it wraps
the spent ask is styled by data-spent, never :disabled: it must answer a fourth press with a note, so it stays pressable and quiet until the hundred words arrive
the strip rests bright (--text-hi) and lights brass on hover; the open-category marker (olive) still wins on an active item
hover is not an act: it lifts to --text-hi, and brass moves to :active, the press
icons and labels 20% larger: 17 to 20.4, 18 to 21.6, 9 to 10.8

the cascade's overlay anchor: absolutely positioned inside the stage (it cannot move the paper), anchored from the strip's right edge because layers grow rightward from the strip; display:flex so docking is ordinary flex reflow. Its left cancels both the host padding and the grid's own centring margin (--fx7-cascade-grid-margin reproduces max(0px, (100vw - 2 x pad - frame-max) / 2)), so it sits on the strip's edge at every viewport (fx7.mjs S3 checks 1100, both reference widths and 2200)
z-index 60: above the drawers (55, 56) in the same isolated stage, so a real press on a cascade row never lands on the Sliver's wrapper; below the dialogs (200 and up)
the drawer sits flush on the rail: no --frame-gap term, pure layout math over the same tokens the strip uses, so it cannot drift from the strip it targets
flush on the rail, the seam is the rail's own border-right: no border-left here (it would read as a hairline gap) and square left corners (a radius at a flush seam is a notch)

the rail pop-outs slide and fade as the Tools strip does, on its tokens (--drawer-dur, --drawer-ease; the short fade alone under reduced motion); backwards fill on the way in; leaving layers take no input; overlay only, nothing moves the page
the cascade drawer's engraved heading: one olive accent per menu, at rest

THEME PICKER (theme-menu-brief.md, theme-rules.md section C): brand cards, not a button list. The card art is never scoped by [data-theme]: a card shows its own theme's look whatever theme is active, so --tp-cyan and --tp-lime are local constants; --brass, theme-invariant, marks the current card

the hover glitch is a flash within the global flash budget: ThemePicker.tsx's controller (store/fluxCardGlitch.ts) asks the budget first and runs this class for one iteration, never an infinite hover loop, and never stacks a second
the theme choice is a choice, not a where-you-are state: a brass outline, theme-invariant

BOARDS CONNECTED (PW1): the Plan panel's connections zone. Its heading reuses the engraved register of .wz-cascade-panel-title; the lexicon carries the words, the register the voice. One accent site per menu, and this is it; no new motion

the two thumbnail shapes: wide for boards, tall for pages, carried by the aspect ratio of a leading swatch (never the row's box), so a long title can wrap without turning a board into a page; no colour, no badge
destructive colour lives only inside the confirm: Delete stays --text-mid like Move; only .wz-cascade-confirm-danger wears --brick

the fold: a header disclosure shared by every list-bearing section (CascadePanels.tsx FoldSection). The whole header is a real full-width button; the chevron is quiet olive at rest and on hover, never brass; keyboard focus keeps the site-wide brass ring, since focus is an event
the text selection is brass from the theme token (selecting is the writer acting), with --on-brass so selected text stays legible; both rules, because Firefox honours only ::selection
six heading levels, one-to-one with h1-h6, each a distinct size, h1 largest and h6 just above body; text-transform:none, so a heading is never forced into capitals

the free-edit surface is one row per line (store/lineRows.ts) with the newline left as text between rows: inline-block, so textContent, innerText and copied text stay identical; contain:layout style keeps a row's layout inside it, and nothing in a row is positioned
no content-visibility on the rows: a skipped row carries no text for innerText, and caret and scroll restores land on estimated rows
the sheet owns a top margin (--ts-top), so the first row is never cut by the page's edge or a scroll; the fields are placed from it and the centred block stays at 40% of the sheet
a leading tab is a first-line indent, one fixed step: tab-size 2em (the default of 8 characters varies with the face); the whole-paragraph indent is the separate block token below

the screenplay surface runs no typewriter: no start offset (it would float a fresh page's caret mid-page) and no fade mask (it would be dead CSS that reanimates if the attribute returned). .mode-scroll and .entry-full keep theirs; the scroll cap's bounded height is the containment fix and stays
the board's name is a button (the rename control) that reads as plain crumb text (the family, size, colour and weight of .crumb-here) with a text cursor, the cue that clicking edits it

in the zoom the ink sheet covers the visible page: it reaches over the scroller's start and end paddings with matching negative margins and paddings, so its text stays put; ink is measured from where the text starts (InkStratum.tsx inkOriginY), so strokes keep their place in both views
the modes move toward the right and Done stays rightmost with a fixed gap, on the framed host only (the legacy sprint-nav layout is untouched); a trial value: delete this block to revert

the deck engine's pop-out (components/DeckWizard.tsx): the same shape as .board-popup-backdrop and .board-popup, so it reads as the pop-out the writer already knows; on a board it reuses .board-canvas-blurred, and CreateProject.tsx, with no board under it, uses the .deck-wizard-blur pair (identical values)
